title: Modi's Historic New Zealand Visit Elevates Ties to Strategic Partnership Amid Rising Anti-Indian Sentiment
excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to New Zealand — the first by an Indian Prime Minister in four decades — has resulted in a significant upgrade of bilateral relations, even as the Indian community navigates rising…
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to New Zealand — the first by an Indian Prime Minister in four decades — has resulted in a significant upgrade of bilateral relations, even as the Indian community navigates rising anti-immigrant sentiment in the Pacific nation.

## Strategic Partnership Elevated

Modi and New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon elevated their nations' diplomatic ties to a "strategic partnership" during talks in Auckland, reflecting "shared democratic values, deep people-to-people links, and shared interests in the Indo-Pacific," according to a joint statement.

The two countries signed a defence cooperation arrangement and pledged greater collaboration on maritime safety, reflecting shared concerns about stability in the Indo-Pacific region. The visit came after Modi signed deals with Indonesia and Australia as part of a broader Asia-Pacific diplomatic push.

## Warm Diaspora Welcome, Complex Undercurrents

The Indian diaspora in New Zealand — approximately 300,000 strong, comprising 143,000 persons of Indian origin and 157,000 Non-Resident Indians — turned out in force to welcome Modi at an Auckland arena. Cultural performances showcasing traditions from Punjab and Tamil Nadu were followed by a fusion of Carnatic and Hindustani classical music and a rendition of Vande Mataram.

"The love and affection of New Zealand's Indian community touched me deeply. They have waited four decades for the visit of an Indian Prime Minister," Modi said on social media.

However, the visit comes against a backdrop of growing tensions. Reuters reported rising anti-Indian sentiment in New Zealand, with Indian residents reporting increased racial abuse. Winston Peters' New Zealand First party has been pushing for tighter migrant controls, and immigration from India has become a flashpoint in the country's political discourse. About 292,000 of New Zealand's 5.3 million people identified as Indian in a 2023 census.

## Broader Asia-Pacific Tour

The New Zealand visit is part of Modi's wider diplomatic tour that included stops in Brazil, Indonesia, and Australia. In Melbourne, the Indian community — the city's largest ethnic minority — expressed optimism about the visit's impact on business and bilateral ties.

"We view PM Modi's visit as something that will significantly boost business and all other aspects of the relationship between India and Australia," said Shivraj Singh, a Melbourne-based Indian restaurant owner.

For the Indian diaspora across the Asia-Pacific, the strategic upgrades and defence cooperation agreements represent concrete steps toward stronger institutional ties — even as questions about community integration and safety persist on the ground.
